<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. XIX.|ACCORDING TO S. MATTHEW.|53}}</noinclude>Natiuitie an Angel for his custodie and Patronage against the wicked before the face of God. ''Hiero. vpon this place''. And the thing is so plaine, that Caluin dare not deny it, and yet he wil needes doubt of it, ''lib. 1. Inst. c. 14. sect.7''.

''17. Not heare the Church.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Disobedience to the Church.}}Not only Heretikes, but any other obstinate offender that wil not be iudged nor ruled by the Church, may be excommunicated, and so made as an Heathen or Publican was to the Iewes, by the discipline of the same, casting him out of the felowship of Catholikes. Which {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Excommunication.}}Excommunication is a greater punishement then if he were executed by sword, fire, and wild beastes. ''Aug. cont. Adu. leg. li. 1. c. 17''. And againe he saith, Man is more sharply and pitefully bound by the Churches Keies, then with any yron or adamantine manicles or fetters in the world. ''August. ibidem''.

''17. Heathen.''] Heretikes therfore because they wil not heare the Church, be no better nor no otherwise to be esteemed of Catholikes, then heathen men and Publicans were esteemed among the Iewes.

''18. You shal binde.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Power to binde and loose.}}As before he gaue this power of binding and loosing ouer the whole, first of al and principally to Peter, vpon whom he builded his Church: so here not only to Peter, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mat. c. 16, 19''.}}and in him to his successors, but also to the other Apostles, and in them to their successors, euery one in their charge. ''Hieron. lib. 1. c. 14. aduers. Iouin. and Epist. ad Heliod. Cyprian. de Vnit. Eccl. nu.3''.

''18. Shal loose.''] Our Lord geueth no lesse right and authoritie to the Churche to loose, then to binde, as S. Ambrose {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Li. 1. de pœnit. c. 2''.}}writeth against the Nouatians, who confessed that the Priests had power to binde, but not to loose.

''20. In the middes of them.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Catholike Assemblies.}}Not al assemblies may chalenge the presence of Christ, but only such as be gathered together in the vnity of the Church. and therfore no conuenticles of Heretikes directly gathering against the Churche, are warranted by this place. ''Cypr. de vnit. Eccles. nu.7. 8''.

''22. Seuentie times seuen.''] There must be no end of forgeuing them that be penitent, either in the Sacrament by absolution, or one man an other their offenses.

{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text={{sc|The fourth}} part of this Gospel, Christs comming into Iurie toward his Passion.}}{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. XIX.}}}}}}

{{c|''He answereth the tempting Pharisees, that the case of a man with his wife shalbe (as in the first institution it was) vtterly indissoluble, though for one cause he may be diuorced. 10 And therevpon to his Disciples he highly commendeth Single life for heauen. 13 He wil haue children come vnto him. 16 He sheweth what is to be done to enter into life euerlasting: 20 What also, for a rich man to be perfect: 27 As also what passing revvard they shal haue which follow that his counsel of perfection: 29 yea though it be but in some one peece.''}} {{verse|chapter=19|verse=1}}AND it came to passe, vvhen {{sc|Iesvs}} had ended these vvordes, he departed from Galilee, & came into the coastes of Ievvrie beyond Iordā,{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 10, 1.''}} {{verse|chapter=19|verse=2}}† and great multitudes folovved him: and he cured them there.

{{verse|chapter=19|verse=3}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel for Mariage. And for S. Agatha Febr. 5.}}And there came to him the Pharisees tempting him, and saying, Is it lavvful for a man to dimisse his vvife, for euery cause? {{verse|chapter=19|verse=4}}† Who ansvvering, said to them, Haue ye not read, that he which did {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''`make man''}}`make' from the beginning, ''made them male and femal''? And he said.{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 1, 27.''}} {{verse|chapter=19|verse=5}}† ''For this cause, man shal leaue father and mother, and shal cleaue to his vvife: and they tvvo shal be in one flesh''.{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 2, 24.''}} {{verse|chapter=19|verse=6}}† Therfore novv they are not two, but one flesh. That therfore vvhich God hath ioyned together, let ‖ not man separate.⊣ {{verse|chapter=19|verse=7}}† They say to him, Why then {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Deut. 24, 1.''}}* did Moyses commaund to giue a bil of diuorce, and to dimisse her? {{verse|chapter=19|verse=8}}† He saith to them, Because Moyses for the hardnes of your hart permitted you to dimisse your vviues:<noinclude>{{rh||G iij|but}}</noinclude>
